source.title_on_document: Human-AI Synergy Supports Collective Creative Search

paper_design_summary: An online experiment compared human social chains, humans working alone, Gemini-only chains, and hybrid human–Gemini chains on a hidden-word guessing task, scoring target similarity and lexical diversity of guesses. The reported human sample was 503 people; rounds within hybrid games were randomly assigned to human or AI players, but allocation of people to the human conditions was not stated (PDF p. 3, Method, Experimental conditions, and Participants and AI queries). Additional model-only controls tested model mixtures, communication formats, and decoding temperatures (PDF pp. 5–6).

studies.label: Main online collective word-guessing experiment; human allocation unstated

assignment.what_was_assigned: Human Social, Human Asocial, and Human-AI Hybrid were compared between conditions. The mechanism allocating people to these conditions is not reported. The explicit randomization concerns whether each round inside a hybrid game is played by a human or a Gemini agent; it does not state random assignment of people to generative-AI assistance.
assignment.quote: within each game, each round was randomly assigned to either a human participant or a Gemini 2.5 Flash agent
assignment.locator: PDF p. 3, Experimental conditions, Human-AI Hybrid description; quoted clause describes assignment of rounds to player type, not assignment of people to conditions.

arms.name: Human Social
arms.description: Different human participants play successive rounds; each may play one round per game in up to 10 games. Human-produced best guesses are passed along the chain (PDF p. 3, Experimental conditions).

arms.name: Human Asocial
arms.description: Each participant is assigned a single game and completes all 10 rounds, totaling 100 guesses (PDF p. 3, Experimental conditions).

arms.name: AI-only
arms.description: All rounds are simulated by Gemini 2.5 Flash agents, with the same best-guess hint, within-round history, and feedback; no human players (PDF p. 3, Experimental conditions).

arms.name: Human-AI Hybrid
arms.description: Each round is randomly allocated to a human or Gemini 2.5 Flash agent; each human plays only one round within a given game and participates in 10 games. Participants are not informed that guesses may come from AI (PDF p. 3, Experimental conditions).

participants.who: Prolific participants based in the US who identified English as their native language. The paper reports 503 successfully recruited participants and condition sample sizes of Human Social N = 210, Human Asocial N = 179, and Human-AI Hybrid N = 114 (PDF p. 3, Experimental conditions and Human participants). These are reported recruitment/condition counts; separate counts at randomization and after exclusions are not stated.
participants.quote: 503 participants were recruited successfully from Prolific
participants.locator: PDF p. 3, Participants and AI queries, Human participants; arm counts in Experimental conditions.

ai_tool.how_used: AI agents produce one-word guesses during their assigned rounds. Best-guess information is passed to subsequent players, providing indirect AI-generated hints to humans in hybrid chains. Temperature 0.7; no direct human chatbot conversation is described (PDF p. 3, Experimental conditions and AI queries).

task.description: Semantle-inspired semantic search for a hidden target word. Each game has 10 rounds of 10 guesses. Players receive Word2Vec cosine-similarity feedback relative to the target, scaled by 201.69, and the best prior-round guess; round maxima and per-game word uniqueness are scored (PDF pp. 3–4, Method, Performance analysis, Diversity analysis).

outcomes.name: Collective search performance: average round-maximum target-similarity score
outcomes.question: with_ai

contrasts.reported: Human-AI Hybrid M = 87.76. The results text reports higher performance than the other conditions, including Human Social (p < .001). For the Hybrid versus Human Social contrast, Figure 3A instead displays **; its caption defines ** as the 0.01 significance level. These conflicting significance descriptions are retained as printed. The Human Social mean is not numerically printed. The score is computed per round and averaged across rounds and games; the hybrid arm includes both human and AI rounds.
contrasts.locator: PDF pp. 3–4, Performance analysis (definition and textual comparison); p. 5, Figure 3A and caption (significance markers), and Controlling for effect of model type and synergy (Hybrid M = 87.76).

outcomes.name: Collective lexical diversity: proportion of unique guessed words within each game
outcomes.question: across_people
outcomes.measure_detail: Lexical diversity is the proportion of unique guessed words within each game, averaged across games (PDF p. 4, Diversity analysis; p. 5, Figure 3C and caption). The Human-AI Hybrid pool includes both human and AI guesses. Figure 3D reports the related cross-game lexical-diversity variant by round; the text describes decreasing diversity over rounds in Human Social and Human-AI Hybrid (PDF p. 4, Diversity analysis; p. 5, Figure 3D and caption).

contrasts.reported: Human-AI Hybrid M = 0.58, reported as lower than the human conditions, including Human Social. Figure 3C marks Human-AI Hybrid versus Human Social with ***; its caption defines *** as the 0.001 significance level and states that only comparisons remaining significant after Bonferroni correction are shown. An exact p value and the Human Social mean are not numerically printed. The measure averages the proportion of unique words within games; hybrid games pool guesses from human and AI players.
contrasts.locator: PDF p. 4, Diversity analysis (Hybrid M = 0.58 and lower diversity than human conditions); p. 5, Figure 3C, Human Social-to-Human-AI Hybrid bracket (***), and Figure 3 caption (significance levels and Bonferroni correction).

diversity_detail.metric: Average proportion of unique guessed words within each game (lexical diversity).
diversity_detail.computed_over: Guessed words pooled within each game, with the within-game unique-word proportion averaged across games in each condition. Human Social games pool different human players; Human-AI Hybrid games pool both human and AI players. Figure 3D additionally reports cross-game lexical diversity at each round.
diversity_detail.uncertainty: Diversity test and uncertainty calculation for Figure 3C-D: not_stated. Figure 3 caption states that only comparisons remaining significant after Bonferroni correction are shown; it specifies participant standard errors for performance panels A and B, not diversity panels C and D.
diversity_detail.notes: This collective measure includes AI-produced guesses in hybrid games and is distinct from the human-only diversity comparison in Figure 4B (S1-O4). Figure 3D is a related cross-game, per-round variant. PDF p. 4, Diversity analysis; p. 5, Figure 3C-D and caption and Figure 4B.

outcomes.name: Human search performance within hybrid versus human-social games
outcomes.question: with_ai

contrasts.reported: Humans in the Human-AI Hybrid condition did not differ significantly in individual performance from the Human Social group: p = 0.392, d = 0.032. This contrast isolates human-produced guesses; the underlying performance score is the maximum target similarity within each round. Arm means are not numerically printed.
contrasts.locator: PDF p. 5, Interaction with people changes AI behavior and Figure 4A; pp. 3–4, Performance analysis (round-maximum score definition).

outcomes.name: Human lexical diversity within hybrid versus human-social games
outcomes.question: across_people
outcomes.measure_detail: Proportion of unique human-produced guessed words, comparing the human subgroup in Human-AI Hybrid with Human Social (PDF p. 5, Figure 4B). The general lexical-diversity metric is defined as the average proportion of unique guessed words within each game (PDF p. 4, Diversity analysis); the exact subgroup aggregation is not separately described.

contrasts.reported: Humans in Human-AI Hybrid contributed a significantly higher proportion of unique words than humans in Human Social: p < .001. Figure 4B, Human panel, marks this comparison with ***; Figure 3 caption defines *** as the 0.001 significance level and states that only comparisons remaining significant after Bonferroni correction are shown throughout the paper. Numerical arm means, SDs, and a numerical confidence interval are not printed. This human-only result is distinct from the lower lexical diversity of the combined human-and-AI pool in S1-O2.
contrasts.locator: PDF p. 5, Interaction with people changes AI behavior, second paragraph; Figure 4B, Human panel, and Figure 4 caption; Figure 3 caption (significance notation and Bonferroni correction). PDF p. 3, Method and Experimental conditions (human-produced best-guess hints in the comparator).

diversity_detail.metric: Proportion of unique human-produced guessed words (lexical diversity).
diversity_detail.computed_over: Human-produced guesses in Human-AI Hybrid compared with human-produced guesses in Human Social; the Figure 4B human comparison excludes AI-produced guesses. The paper defines the general metric within games and averages across games, but does not separately specify subgroup denominator handling or aggregation.
diversity_detail.uncertainty: Diversity test and error-bar calculation: not_stated. Figure 3 caption states that only comparisons surviving Bonferroni correction are shown throughout the paper; Figure 4B marks the human comparison with ***.
diversity_detail.notes: A comparison across human players, distinct from the mixed human-and-AI pool in S1-O2. The participant standard-error descriptions in Figure 3 explicitly concern performance panels A and B; the paper does not give a separate uncertainty method for this diversity comparison. PDF p. 4, Diversity analysis; p. 5, Interaction with people changes AI behavior, Figure 4B and caption, and Figure 3 caption.

studies.label: AI model-type and model-mixture control experiment

assignment.what_was_assigned: Model composition of AI-only games: Gemini alone, GPT alone, or a Gemini/GPT mixture. No new people are assigned in these model-only conditions; random allocation of AI models is not stated. Comparisons to human conditions reuse S1.
assignment.quote: we implemented a Hybrid AI condition consisting of Gemini 2.5 Flash (50%) and GPT 5.1 (50%) agents
assignment.locator: PDF p. 5, Controlling for effect of model type and synergy.

arms.description: New experiment with GPT 5.1 alone (PDF p. 5).

arms.name: Hybrid AI
arms.description: Mixture of Gemini 2.5 Flash (50%) and GPT 5.1 (50%) agents (PDF p. 5).

participants.who: AI agents only in the new control conditions; no additional human sample. The original Gemini-only baseline and human-hybrid comparison come from S1.
participants.quote: we implemented a Hybrid AI condition consisting of Gemini 2.5 Flash (50%) and GPT 5.1 (50%) agents
participants.locator: PDF p. 5, Controlling for effect of model type and synergy.

ai_tool.how_used: Autonomous word-guessing agents are compared individually by model and in mixed-model chains. Both use temperature 0.7; GPT 5.1 uses medium reasoning effort (PDF p. 3, AI queries; p. 5, Controlling for effect of model type and synergy).

task.description: The same hidden-word semantic-search task, evaluating performance and lexical diversity of AI-only games (PDF pp. 5–6, Controlling for effect of model type and synergy).

studies.label: AI-only prompt and social-information control experiments

assignment.what_was_assigned: AI-only conditions vary the information passed between successive agents: the main best-guess hint, full history, single-word advice, or multi-sentence advice. No human allocation is involved; random allocation of AI conditions is not stated.
assignment.quote: We conducted additional AI-only control experiments to assess the robustness of our main findings to variation in prompt design, social information format, and model decoding temperature.
assignment.locator: PDF p. 6, Controlling for prompts and social information.

arms.name: Best-guess baseline (from S1)
arms.description: Main Gemini-only condition passing the best-guess signal between rounds (PDF p. 6).

arms.name: Complete History
arms.description: Agents receive the full guessing history of previous players (PDF p. 6).

arms.name: Short Advice
arms.description: Agents receive and pass on a single-word piece of advice (PDF p. 6).

arms.name: Long Advice
arms.description: Agents exchange multi-sentence natural-language advice (PDF p. 6).

participants.who: AI-only control experiments; no human participants.
participants.quote: We conducted additional AI-only control experiments to assess the robustness of our main findings to variation in prompt design, social information format, and model decoding temperature.
participants.locator: PDF p. 6, Controlling for prompts and social information.

ai_tool.how_used: AI-only word-guessing agents with modified inter-agent information; the main AI-only model is identified on PDF p. 3, and communication variations are described on p. 6.

task.description: Hidden-word semantic-search games with different inter-agent communication formats; performance is compared with the main AI-only condition (PDF p. 6, Controlling for prompts and social information).

eligibility.reason: Random assignment is stated for rounds to human or AI players within hybrid games, but allocation of people to Human Social, Human Asocial, or Human-AI Hybrid is not stated; criterion 1 remains unclear (PDF p. 3, Experimental conditions). The paper reports 503 successfully recruited people and condition sample sizes of 210 Social, 179 Asocial, and 114 Hybrid, but no separate analyzed counts; criterion 2 is therefore unclear despite every reported human condition sample exceeding 50 (PDF p. 3, Experimental conditions and Human participants). Target similarity and lexical diversity are computed on produced guesses, including separate human-only performance and diversity comparisons, so criterion 3 is met (PDF pp. 3-5, Performance analysis, Diversity analysis, and Figure 4A-B). Core eligibility remains unclear, with context_class none because neither randomized nor nonrandom allocation of people is established. The single-target convergent task and the pooling of human and AI guesses in collective outcomes remain scope considerations; the human-only outcomes are recorded separately. Model-only controls add no human sample (PDF pp. 5-6, control experiments).

one_line_finding: Hybrid groups had the highest search performance (M = 87.76), while humans in hybrid games had higher lexical diversity (p < .001) but no significant performance difference from Human Social (p = 0.392, d = 0.032; PDF p. 5, Interaction with people changes AI behavior, Figure 4A-B, and Controlling for effect of model type and synergy).
